 Govt to consider extending flood aid to petty traders
 By DIVYA THERESA RAVI  and  RAGANANTHINI VETHASALAM 
 Thursday, 19 Nov 2026
 | 11:05 AM MYT

  KUALA LUMPUR: A proposal to extend flood aid to affected small traders will be brought to the Central Disaster Management Committee for consideration, says Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi.
 Datuk Mohd Isam Mohd Isa (BN-Tampin) asked in the Dewan Rakyat if the government would shift its aid assessment from temporary flood relief centre registration to verified disaster damage, arguing that the current system excludes stranded victims and petty traders.
 "Currently, we disburse compassionate cash aid (Bantuan Wang Ihsan) before flood victims return home. That means we try our best to get it to them while they are still at the relief centre," Ahmad Zahid said in reply on Thursday (Nov 19).
 "For those who do not evacuate to a relief centre but are affected, for example, those staying at their children's or other relatives' homes, we will provide them the aid as long as they are registered at the flood victim registration centre."
 Separately, he said 159 non-governmental organisations (NGOs) nationwide are on standby to assist flood victims during the ongoing North-East Monsoon season.
 Wan Razali Wan Nor (PN-Kuantan) asked about the government's preparedness in terms of rescue teams, asset readiness and welfare assistance, including financial aid, during the ongoing monsoon.
 Ahmad Zahid added that non-uniformed NGOs are coordinated by the Social Welfare Department under the disaster management framework.
 Wan Razali also asked about the mechanism for coordinating volunteers and NGOs, the National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma)’s operational allocation nationwide and for Pahang, particularly Kuantan; as well as the involvement of elected representatives regardless of political affiliation in disaster response efforts.
 "This is based on Nadma Directive No. 1 on the national disaster management policy and mechanism," Ahmad Zahid replied.
 "Coordination has been carried out at all levels, including with NGOs mobilised by political parties, regardless of political affiliation.
 "For Kuantan specifically, and the state of Pahang in general, we have mobilised all assets... let us set aside political differences in this matter because floods do not recognise political colours."
